usageNotes: Issues an immediate hard stop of a QEMU VM by terminating the qemu process — equivalent to a power cut; use only when the guest OS is unresponsive or a graceful shutdown (post_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_status_shutdown) has failed. The call is asynchronous and returns a task UPID; poll the task endpoint to confirm completion. Requires VM.PowerMgmt on /vms/{vmid}; the node must be online and reachable.

examples.summary: Force-stop a hung VM (ID 105) on node pve1, overriding any in-progress shutdown task

destructiveReason: Terminates the QEMU process without flushing disk write buffers or notifying the guest OS, which can corrupt in-flight I/O and leave the VM's filesystem in an inconsistent state.
tips: Prefer post_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_status_shutdown for any VM whose guest OS is still responsive — it triggers a clean ACPI shutdown.
Set overrule-shutdown: true when a previous qmshutdown task is stuck; otherwise the stop may be blocked waiting for it to finish.
keepActive: true prevents Proxmox from deactivating storage volumes after the stop — useful during live migration teardown or when another process needs the volumes to remain mounted.
skiplock is root-only and should be treated as a last resort; holding locks usually signals another operation is in progress.
The returned UPID can be polled via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to confirm the stop completed before starting dependent operations.
